Messages.Author: candl...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
This happened last night and we needed some clarification: Vittorio
Giovanni used clan impersonation to become a Lasombra, but as he didn't
want to be a Sabbat (as Hannibal was in the game) he decided to be a
Lasombra Independent like Lucita. Is this fair? Could he then use Clan
Loyalty so that Lasombras can't block?

And, if this is the case, could a vampire become a Malkavian Antitribu
Independent or a Toreador Independent or a Ravnos Camarilla?

Thanks!

Sent via Deja.com
http://www.deja.com/

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
candl...@my-deja.com wrote:
> This happened last night and we needed some clarification: Vittorio
> Giovanni used clan impersonation to become a Lasombra, but as he
> didn't want to be a Sabbat (as Hannibal was in the game) he decided to
> be a Lasombra Independent like Lucita. Is this fair? Could he then use
> Clan Loyalty so that Lasombras can't block?

When he switches clans to a clan of a different sect,
he switches sects as well. He's Sabbat, whether he wants
to be or not. [10]

> And, if this is the case, could a vampire become a Malkavian Antitribu
> Independent or a Toreador Independent or a Ravnos Camarilla?

Ravnos Camarilla is possible with a Writ of Acceptance or a
successful Ravnos Acceptance referendum. The others are not
possible under the current card set.

Yes. (Whilst the vampire remains Sabbat. Once they become Camarilla
again, they can pick it up again, assuming they haven't been forced to
relinquish it.)

>Can I play a Clan Impersonation and chose to become one of the Independent
>Antitribu clans (eg !Ravnos), i'm guessing not. but you never know. Maybe
>it's only possible if these clans are releases (hint hint)

There are no !Ravnos in V:TES, so no. You must pick a clan that's in
the game.

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <20010104231847...@ng-cr1.aol.com>,

halc...@aol.com (Halcyan 2) wrote:
> What if a Camarilla vampire equips with a Writ of Acceptance
> and then gets Deranged? Does the Derange override the effect
> of the Writ, or does the Writ modify sect status after the
> Derange effect is factored in?

The Derange makes the vampire a Malkavian Antitribu, and the
Writ keeps it a member of the Camarilla.

The vampire becomes a Camarilla Malkavian Antitribu.

Derange does not specify anything about sect, so only effects
the sect of the victim when other effects are not in play
(ie, Writ of Acceptance).

Carpe Noctem.
